value: This research explores the intersection of programming languages and software engineering, investigating how software expression influences its engineerability at scale, with a core focus on improving software quality and programmer productivity. This is achieved through novel methods for expressing structural and behavioral design within source code, with key contributions including work on object-oriented typestate checking, modular and gradual verification techniques for stateful and aspect-oriented programs, and new object-oriented language models. This work, particularly in specifying and verifying software architecture, has been recognized with awards such as the NSF CAREER award and the Dahl-Nygaard Junior Prize, and underpins a diverse portfolio of active and past projects spanning dynamic analysis, gradual verification, domain-specific language design, and educational tools for language metatheory.
